note: Absolute forecast error as a percentage of monthly revenue. Each run is 12 backtests (4 sellers x 30/45/60-day horizons). 'baseline' uses data generated by the same process the forecaster assumes, so it is a consistency check rather than evidence of real-world accuracy. The other rows deliberately break an assumption. In the late-payout rows every payout releases the sales it was scheduled to release but lands 0-3 days late; a payout pushed past the end of the history stays pending. Those rows repeat the run over 100 independent sets of draws, one seeded generator per seller. Late payouts are the dominant sensitivity, and the error is concentrated (see by_payout_position): it is large when a payout is due on the day the forecast is measured and arrives late, and close to the baseline otherwise. A payout that is late on the day the forecast is MADE no longer hurts: the forecaster notices it is missing from the bank ledger and expects it. The what-if simulator's 'payouts arrive late' setting exists so a seller can test exactly this on their own projection.
